description: Realistic, drivable 5G remote-driving latency from the FULL N-HiTS pipeline (paper methodology, end-to-end): a real N-HiTS model trained on the public 0913ktg/5G-Traffic-Generator youtubeLive uplink dataset (72k samples) generates a 60k-sample UL bitrate trace (data/5g_generated/scm_youtubeLive_ul_real), mapped through the queue-load model with the traffic SCALE calibrated so the real bursts actually create congestion (peak load ~0.9, not the smoke trace's 0.22). Generated one-way distribution: command/uplink p50 31 ms, p95 95 ms, handover spikes to 350 ms; camera/downlink p50 97 ms, p95 170 ms, spikes to 600 ms. Two brief (0.4-0.5 s) handover outages, no sustained outage -> stays drivable. control=uplink command, camera=downlink video (independent channel, not a scaled copy), manual mirrors control. Supersedes the calibrated-lognormal 5g_realistic.json stopgap; the harsher autonomous-sweep profile keeps the full outage.
